stemMd: Where does glycolysis occur in a typical human cell?

options.label: E
options.textMd: On the outer surface of the plasma membrane

explanationMd: Glycolysis converts glucose to pyruvate through reactions in the cytosol. It does not require mitochondria to carry out its own steps. Later aerobic processing of pyruvate and oxidative phosphorylation involve mitochondria in human cells.

distractorRationale.a: This membrane houses the respiratory electron transport chain, not glycolysis.
distractorRationale.b: Glycolysis is a cytosolic metabolic pathway.
distractorRationale.e: Glycolytic reactions occur inside the cell.
